title: Anatomy of a Rust Desk application

boxes.label: An app model
boxes.sub: what an app is, and how it runs
boxes.text: Open design question. The documents sketch apps as modules behind a C-compatible SDK; nothing implements it on the native track.

boxes.label: The SDK ABI (desk_*)
boxes.text: The interface apps would use to talk to the Desk. Specified in a document; no app calls it.

boxes.label: Windows owned by apps
boxes.text: In the first window the scenario, run by the shell, opens both windows. No app owns a window yet.

boxes.label: System calls
boxes.text: The kernel has no user mode, no task-state segment and no system-call gate: everything runs in one flat address space as one program.

boxes.label: Executable format and loader
boxes.sub: DXE3 only on the hosted track
boxes.text: The hosted track proved loading a Rust module with DJGPP's DXE3 format. A native loader needs a format it can load without DJGPP's runtime; that is an open question, planned after live input.

boxes.label: Tasks, scheduling, memory protection
boxes.text: Cooperative in one address space or preemptive processes is an open question, and so is paging.

boxes.label: desk-wm
boxes.text: Windows, z-order, focus, hit testing, dragging and the damage each change makes.

boxes.label: desk-shell
boxes.text: The Shell value: handle(event) and frame(), plus the scenario runner.

boxes.label: desk-ui, desk-font
boxes.text: Theme roles, window chrome, text and the .DFN reader.

boxes.label: desk-gfx
boxes.text: Surfaces, damage, the compositor, the Present trait and the digests.

boxes.label: The platform owns the loop
boxes.sub: it calls Shell::handle and Shell::frame; the core never calls the machine
boxes.text: The seam the first window uses instead of a general Platform trait: each platform runs its own loop and hands the core events, then presents the frame's damage.

boxes.label: desk-present
boxes.text: The presenters that turn damage into writes to a frame buffer or to the VGA planes.

boxes.label: desk-hal
boxes.text: The traits the core and the drivers are written against, tested on the host with a mock platform.

boxes.label: Drivers
boxes.text: Shared drivers, tested on the host and in the emulators.

boxes.label: Live input into the shell
boxes.sub: DOS keys only; no mouse, no native
boxes.text: Both tracks have input drivers. The comparison runs hand the shell scripted events; only on DOS were keys typed through IRQ 1 into the focused field (an interactive run in DOSBox). The mouse reached the shell on neither track, and nothing live reached the native shell; the live-input task is separate and optional.

boxes.label: Native: kernel/src/shell.rs
boxes.sub: the kernel's shell test mode, in QEMU
boxes.text: The kernel runs the scenario and QEMU's screendumps are compared with the goldens.

boxes.label: Hosted: shell/dos, SHELL.EXE
boxes.sub: the same core on DOS, in DOSBox
boxes.text: SHELL.EXE runs the same core on the pure-Rust DOS runtime; its read-back is compared with the goldens.

boxes.label: Boot sector and loader
boxes.text: Real mode to protected mode, then the kernel; booted in QEMU, Bochs and 86Box.

boxes.label: The kernel's services
boxes.sub: GDT, IDT, heap, frames, BIOS calls
boxes.text: What exists today under the first window: memory, interrupts, a timer, the BIOS trampoline and the drivers.

boxes.label: FreeDOS for DOS programs
boxes.text: Running DOS programs on the native OS is planned by bundling FreeDOS.

boxes.label: QEMU (-cpu 486) and DOSBox Staging
boxes.text: Everything above was run here, and in no other emulator for the first window.

boxes.label: A real 486 PC
boxes.text: No real hardware has been used.
